previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, type II diabetes, and a history of recurrent dialysis line infections was admitted after her hemodialysis catheter clotted during a routine session. She reported feeling generally unwell and mildly short of breath but denied fever or other acute symptoms. A temporary femoral line was placed in the emergency department, and alteplase was administered to restore function to the occluded catheter, which was successful. She remained afebrile with negative blood cultures and continued her six-week course of intravenous vancomycin for MRSA vertebral osteomyelitis diagnosed in a prior admission. Chest imaging showed no pulmonary edema or infection. Her dialysis access was restored without surgical intervention, and she completed a dialysis session before discharge. She was transferred to extended care to complete her antibiotic therapy with outpatient follow-up planned.
problems: Other complications due to renal dialysis device, implant, and graft

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ female with infected left Perm-A-Cath, rule out
pneumonia.

COMPARISON:  ___.

PORTABLE SEMI-UPRIGHT CHEST, ONE VIEW:  A left-sided dialysis catheter
terminates in the cavo-atrial junction, unchanged.  The heart size is in the
upper limits of normal.  Otherwise, hilar, and mediastinal contours are
unremarkable. The lungs are grossly clear without focal consolidation or
pulmonary edema. There is no pleural effusion or pneumothorax.  Osseous
structures are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:  No acute cardiopulmonary process.

HISTORY:  ___ female with end-stage renal disease and recent line
infection, requiring hemodialysis line placement.

COMPARISON:  None available.

RADIOLOGISTS:  The procedure was performed by Drs. ___ with Dr.
___ Attending ___, supervising the entire procedure. Dr.
___ has reviewed this study.

PROCEDURE:  Following explanation of the risk, benefits, and alternatives to
the procedure, written informed consent was obtained.  The patient was placed
on the angiography table supine and the right neck and chest were prepped and
draped in standard sterile fashion.  Using ultrasound guidance, the right
internal jugular vein was punctured.  However, was not possible to pass the
wire into the ___, as the right internal jugular vein was occluded with
thrombus, demonstrated on multiple ultrasound images.  At this point, it was
decided to attempt on the left side.

The left neck and chest were prepped and draped in the standard sterile
fashion.  Following a second preprocedure timeout, ultrasound guidance was
used to puncture the left internal jugular vein.  However, it was again not
possible to pass a 0.018 nitinol wire.  At this point, a small amount of
contrast was injected, and a left internal jugular venogram demonstrated
occlusion of the left internal jugular vein, with only tiny collateral vessel
flow not amenable to catheter placement.  At this point, the patient's primary
team (Dr. ___ was contacted, and the options were discussed.
It was decided to attempt a right femoral temporary line.

After explanation of the change in procedure plan to the patient the right
groin was prepped and draped in standard sterile fashion. Using ultrasound
guidance, the right femoral vein was punctured and a 0.018 nitinol wire was
advanced into the right common iliac vein under fluoroscopic guidance. Hard
copy ultraound images were obtained before and after venous access documenting
vessel patency. The needle was exchanged for a peel- away sheath. A 24 cm
temporary dual- lumen hemodialysis catheter was then advanced under
fluoroscopic guidance into the IVC.  The sheeth was removed, the ports were
flushed and hep-locked, and the line was secured to the skin with an adhesive
sterile device.  The patient tolerated the procedure well with no immediate
complications.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Occluded right internal jugular vein.

2.  Occlusion of distal left internal jugular vein near the confluence with
the left subclavian vein with tiny collateral venous circulation that is not
amenable to catheter placement.

3.  Successful placement of temporary hemodialysis catheter via right femoral
vein approach.

These findings were discussed with Dr. ___ at 1:00 p.m. on
___.

HISTORY:  Line infection and chest pain.

FINDINGS:  In comparison with study of ___, the left-sided dialysis catheter
has been removed.  The cardiac silhouette remains at the upper limits of
normal or slightly enlarged.  No definite evidence of vascular congestion or
pleural effusion or acute pneumonia.

PATIENT HISTORY:  ___ woman with end-stage renal disease and line
infection in need of a new dialysis catheter and occluded internal jugular.
Please evaluate for pre-recanalization planning for internal jugular veins.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial images were obtained from the aortic arch to the
orbits.  Intravenous contrast material was injected, and delayed venous phase
images were obtained.  Images were processed to provide coronal, sagittal, and
axial MIPs.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS:  There is occlusion of the inferior two-thirds of the right internal
jugular vein.  There is also occlusion of the inferior 3 cm of the left
internal jugular vein.

There is calcified plaque in the aortic arch. The distal left common carotid
artery is medialized. There is calcified plaque without evidence
hemodynamically significant stenoses in both internal carotid arteries. There
is calcified plaque in the proximal V2 segments of both vertebral arteries.

There is calcified plaque without evidence of hemodynamically significant
stenoses in the cavernous and supraclinoid internal carotid arteries. This
study was not targed for the evaluation of the circle of ___.

The pulmonary artery is enlarged measuring 4 cm in diameter, suggestive of
moderate pulmonary hypertension.

The thyroid is enlarged with multiple calcified and noncalcified nodules.
There is mild dependent atelectasis in imaged upper lungs.  There is fluid in
some of the lateral mastoid air cells bilaterally. There is degenerative
disease of the cervical spine.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Occlusion of the inferior two-thirds of the right internal jugular and the
inferior 3 cm of the left internal jugular.

2.  Enlarged thyroid with calcified and noncalcified nodules.  Further
evaluation by ultrasound is recommended, if not performed previously.

3.  Moderate enlargement of the pulmonary artery, suggestive of pulmonary
hypertension.

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  ___ woman with end-stage renal disease.  She
currently has a right femoral venous non-tunneled catheter.  Request is made
for permanent tunneled access.

ANESTHESIA:  MAC anesthesia was provided by the anesthesia department. 1%
lidocaine and 1% lidocaine with epinephrine was used for local anesthesia.

OPERATORS:  ___, M.D. and ___, M.D., the attending
physician, who was present for the entire procedure. Dr. ___ this
study.

PROCEDURE AND FINDINGS:  After review of the risks and benefits of the
procedure, informed consent was obtained.  The patient was brought to the
angiography suite and placed supine on the imaging table.  Ultrasound
evaluation of the neck demonstrated a patent left external jugular vein.  The
left neck was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  Access was
obtained with ultrasound into the left external jugular vein with the
micropuncture needle. Hard-copy ultrasound images were obtained before and
after access.  An 018 wire was passed through the micropuncture needle into
the SVC under flouroscopic guidance.  A small skin incision was made over the
needle and the needle was withdrawn and replaced with the micropuncture
sheath.  The inner stiffener and wire were removed and replaced with a short
___ wire.

Next, a subcutaneous tunnel was created on the left anterior superior chest
wall.  The dialysis catheter was pulled through the tunnel and out the
venotomy site.  A long peel-away sheath was placed over the ___ wire.
However, it could not be advanced beyond the confluence of the left innominate
vein and SVC.  The sheath was removed.  A Kumpe catheter was placed over the
___ wire into the IVC.  The ___ wire was removed and replaced with the
stiffer Amplatz wire.  The peel-away sheath was then placed over the Amplatz
wire into the right atrium.  The wire and stiffener were removed and the
dialysis catheter was placed through the sheath as the sheath was peeled away.
The dialysis catheter is a 15.5 ___ x 27 cm length tip- to-cuff catheter.
Its tip is in the superior right atrium. Both ports flushed and aspirated
well. A sterile dressing was applied after the access site was closed with ___
Vicryl suture and the catheter was sutured to the skin with 0 silk. There were
no immediate complications.

At this point, the right groin temporary catheter was removed and a sterile
dressing was applied.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Placement of 27-cm tip-to-cuff angiodynamics dialysis catheter via the
left external jugular vein with the tip in the superior right atrium.
2.  Removal of right groin temporary catheter.
